---
title: "Background & Career"
subtitle: "From Rosario to global stardom"
---

## Early Life

Lionel Andrés Messi was born on June 24, 1987, in Rosario, Santa Fe, Argentina, the third of four children. He began playing football as a young child with his local club, Grandoli, coached by his father, Jorge Messi.

At age 11, Messi was diagnosed with a growth-hormone deficiency, a condition that required expensive treatment his family struggled to afford. This medical challenge became a turning point in his career: FC Barcelona, impressed by his talent, offered to cover the cost of his treatment if his family relocated to Spain — an offer his family accepted in 2000.

## Rise Through La Masia

Messi joined FC Barcelona's famed youth academy, La Masia, where he progressed rapidly through the club's youth ranks. He made his first-team debut for Barcelona in October 2004 at age 17, quickly establishing himself as an integral part of the squad.

## Club Career

**FC Barcelona (2004–2021)**
Messi spent the majority of his career at Barcelona, becoming the club's all-time leading scorer and helping the team win numerous domestic and international trophies, including multiple UEFA Champions League titles. He formed a devastating attacking partnership with players like Xavi, Andrés Iniesta, and later Luis Suárez and Neymar as part of the celebrated "MSN" trio.

**Paris Saint-Germain (2021–2023)**
In August 2021, Messi moved to Paris Saint-Germain, where he continued to add domestic silverware to his trophy cabinet while adapting to a new league and system.

**Inter Miami CF (2023–present)**
In 2023, Messi joined Inter Miami CF in Major League Soccer, a move that generated significant global attention for American soccer and helped drive record interest, attendance, and merchandise sales for the league.

## International Career

Messi made his debut for the Argentina national team in 2005 and has gone on to become the country's most-capped player and all-time leading goalscorer. After several near-misses in major finals, he captained Argentina to victory at the **2021 Copa América** and the **2022 FIFA World Cup** in Qatar — a tournament widely considered the crowning achievement of his career, delivered on a dramatic penalty-shootout final against France.

## Career Timeline

| Year | Milestone |
|------|-----------|
| 1987 | Born in Rosario, Argentina |
| 2000 | Moves to Spain to join FC Barcelona's youth academy |
| 2004 | Makes senior debut for FC Barcelona |
| 2005 | Debuts for the Argentina national team |
| 2009 | Wins first Ballon d'Or |
| 2021 | Wins Copa América with Argentina; transfers to Paris Saint-Germain |
| 2022 | Wins the FIFA World Cup with Argentina |
| 2023 | Joins Inter Miami CF in Major League Soccer |
